 Aged about 31 years,

R/at : Hallekote Hobli,

(By Sri.Prasanna. G.R, Adv)

 SCCH-23  2 MVC No.987/2024 RESPONDENT/S: Sri. Srinivasaiah,

 Siddenahalli, Kottagalu,
 Ramanagara-562117.
 (By Sri.G.S.Manjunath, Advocate)
JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a RTA.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that on 23.10.2023 at about 6.30 a.m, the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-13-EW-3735 in slowly, cautiously by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

When he reached near Swamy Home, Siddenahalli village, Harohalli Nagendra vs Srinivasaiah on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127711238/
1 Hobli and Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time the driver of Tractor and Trailer bearing Reg.No.KA-50-8435 and KA-50-8436, which was coming from opposite direction at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to the said impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Dayananda Sagar Hospital, wherein he took first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to SCCH-23 Confido Multi Speciality Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and he was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
He has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that due to the said accident he lost his earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor and Trailer.
The respondent being the owner is liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent, respondent appeared through his counsel by filing written statement contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
This respondent has denied rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tractor and Trailer.

Per contra he contended that the the petitioner was riding the motorcycle under the influence of alcohol and without observing and following the traffic rules he suddenly enter into the main road from the cross road and dashed against the Tractor and Trailer.
SCCH-23
Hence the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and he was the sole and main architect for the alleged accident.
The respondent admitted that he is the RC owner of the Tractor and trailer.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 23-10-2023 at about 06.30 AM, near Siddenahalli Village, near Swamy Home, Harohalli Hobli and Taluk, Ramanagar, due to rash and negligent driving of Tractor bearing Reg. No.KA-50- 8435 and Trolley bearing Reg.No.KA-50-8436 and caused accident as mentioned in claim petition?

? 
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
5. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 14 were marked on his behalf.

Dr.
Ramachandra examined as PW.2, through him got marked Ex.P.15 & 16.

The respondent SCCH-23 Nagendra vs Srinivasaiah on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127711238/
2

being the owner of the Tractor and Trailer himself examined as RW.1.
6.
Heard both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 7. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.80 lakhs together.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver and owner of the Tractor and Trailer for the offences punishable under section's 279, 338 of IPC and u/s 180, 181, 196, 187 of IMV Act.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
The respondent contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner as he was consumed alcohol and hence he was the main architect to the alleged accident.

In SCCH-23 order to prove the defence the respondent being the owner of the tractor and trailer himself examined as RW.1 and during the course of his cross-examination he categorically admitted that at the time of accident his brother was driving the Tractor and was aged 19 to 20 years.
Further he stated that at the time of accident he was also in the tractor, but in the said police documents it has not mentioned about he was in the tractor.
Further he categorically admitted there is no record of the applicant being drunk, either in the police records or in the hospital records.
Further the respondent has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
Therefore, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the Tractor and trailer.

Therefore, this Tribunal answers Issue No.1 'In the Affirmative'.
8. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable SCCH-23 negligence of the driver of the Tractor and Trailer.
Therefore he is entitled for compensation.
9. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :

The petitioner has exhibited his Aadhar card at Ex.P6,
wherein his date of birth is reflected as 01.01.1992.
This indicates that he was aged (31 years 9 months 22 days) 32 years on the date of accident.
No documents have been produced to establish the avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in his evidence affidavit.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated. 05.07.2023.

Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.

To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on Nagendra vs Srinivasaiah on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127711238/
3 record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the SCCH-23 claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred in the year 2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.

10. As per the medical records and evidence of doctor, petitioner has sustained the following injuries : 1) Traumatic crush injury 2) Type-III C compound comminuted right both bones (Tibia and fibula)
fracture with neurovascular injury 3) Right Gangrenous Lower extremity.
It is needless to say that the injuries are grievous in nature.
The discharge summary Ex.P.8 indicates that the petitioner was taken treatment as an inpatient from 24.10.2023 to 06.11.2023 for a period of 14 days.

During the course of treatment he undergone surgeries in the form of : 1) Wound debridement with vascular repair of posterior tibial artery with fibula graft for right tibia fracture SCCH-23 with external fixation done under SA on 24.10.2023 2) Right above knee amputation done under SA on 31.10.2023.
11. It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has thereby lost his earning capacity.
Therefore he got examined Dr.Ramachandra as PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained right above knee amputation.
As per the Discharge summary the petitioner was underwent surgeries and underwent above knee amputation.

On clinical examination he found that the petitioner has suffered disability to right lower limb below the level of lower one third of the right thigh are absent or missing due to post above knee amputation, scants due to traumatic crush injury of right leg resulting in Gangrene and amputation.

He stated that right lower limb was absent below the level of Middle one third lower one third of right thigh giving rise to 85% of disability of right lower limb, if when converted to whole body it will be 43% of disability.
The recent X-ray shows soft tissues and bones of the right lower limb SCCH-23 below the level of junction of Middle 1/3rd and lower 1/3rd of the Right thigh are absent or missing due to amputation.
Further the petitioner was clinically and radiologically examined and the assessment of disability was done as per the Central Government Notification.
Further he found that petitioner has sustained permanent residual physical disability of about 85% of right lower limb which is about 43% of whole body.

During the course of his cross-examination he admitted that he has not treated the petitioner and was assessed the disability on the basis of medical examination, x-rays and based on Gazette Notification.
He denied the suggestions with regard to the assessment of disability.
However, from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the physical disability.
It is not functional disability.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Nagendra vs Srinivasaiah on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127711238/
4
Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

By SCCH-23 applying the said precedent to the present case on hand, from the petition averments it could be culled out that petitioner was 31 years age old has lost his leg and because of this he may suffer huge pain and embarrassment in the society.
The petitioner has to depend on some one for his livelihood.

He was doing JCB Operator and driver, when such is the case with a injuries sustained by the petitioner he cannot do his work in life long, as such his efficiency in work will decrease and it indirectly affect his income.
Whereas the petitioner can develop the new skills and opt for career transition.
The record reveals that the petitioner was working as JCB Operator and due to the accidental injuries he lost his leg.

A right above-knee amputation (AKA) causes significant, often total, disruption to the ability to work as a JCB (backhoe loader) operator, primarily due to the loss of natural leg function required for controlling machinery, maintaining balance, and maneuvering in a construction environment.
The loss of the right leg means the operator cannot actuate these pedals, rendering standard machines inoperable.
For a driver loosing his right leg is a great SCCH-23 set back.
For the rest of his life he has to work without his right leg.
In many cases, courts have recognized this injury as leading to a 100% loss of earning capacity for drivers.

Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 100%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, this Tribunal consider the functional disability of the petitioner at 100%.
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Tractor and Trailer.

Therefore he is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
12. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES :
The period of hospitalization of 14 days is proved.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at SCCH-23 Rs.1,200/- per day and a sum of Rs.16,800/- (1,200 X 14) is awarded under this head.
13. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
The documents discloses that petitioner had sustained injury to (i) right above knee amputation.
The petitioner has to suffer this unbearable pain of amputation.
Having regard to the fractures and amputation of the leg suffered by the petitioner to weight bearing bones and such other attending circumstances.

Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.3,00,000/-
under this head.

14. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD:
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment given and duration of his stay in the hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 8 months.

Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner,
this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.1,28,000/-
Nagendra vs Srinivasaiah on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127711238/
5 (16,000 X 8) under this head.
SCCH-23 15.
MEDICAL EXPENSES :

As per the bills marked at Ex.P9, the petitioner has spent Rs.3,98,757/-
towards medical expenses.
During the course of his cross-examination PW.1 admitted that the respondent has paid Rs.1,00,000/- for hospital expenses.
As per the admission the respondent has paid Rs.1,00,000/- to the petitioner and same was deducted from the medical bills award amount.

The petitioner has also produced 4- bills same was issued by The Association of People with Disability for a sum of Rs.39,190/- which are marked at Ex.P.12 and date of bills was mentioned as 30.08.2024, 11.09.2024 and 28.11.2024.
It is pertinent to note that the accident was occurred on 23.10.2023, the Ex.P.12 bills dates shows the date after one year of the accident.
Hence the petitioner has not stated that what purpose the Ex.P.12 was produced and he has also not produced the prescriptions of doctor to prove the same.
Hence the bills produced at Ex.P.12 was not considered.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of his cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for (Rs.3,98,757 - SCCH-23 Rs.1,00,000) = Rs.2,98,757/- which is rounded off to Rs.2,98,800/- towards medical expenses.
16. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '16' as the petitioner was aged about 31 years.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Hence a sum of Rs.30,72,000/-
(Rs.16,000 X 12 X 16 X 100%) is awarded under this head.
17. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
As per the medical records the petitioner was aged 31 years at the time of accident.
His right above knee is amputed.
At such unfortunately he has suffered 100% permanent physical disability to the whole body.
Hence he will not only face difficulties in performing his day today activities but will also not be able to enjoy his rest of the life to its fullest extent.

Therefore it would be just and reasonable to award a sum of Rs.1,50,000/-
under this head.
18. FUTURE PROSPECTS:
The accident & resultant amputation of right leg would definitely hamper the petitioner's SCCH-23 prospect of getting any employment in future.
Someway or the other the amputation would affect his future prospects both professionally and personally.
For the loss that the petitioner shall suffer in this regard ends of justice would be met if he is awarded a compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under this head.
19. FUTURE MEDICAL & OTHER INCIDENTAL EXPENSES:

The doctor witness stated that the petitioner has to needs artificial leg synthetic modular and computer assisted design, which is durable long lasting and expensive, as patient says he was a JCB operator.
No estimation is produced to show the future medical expenses.
In this context what deserves notice is that with technological advancement the quality of artificial limbs has improved and these advanced artificial limbs do come at a substantive price.

Further like any other machinery they also require Nagendra vs Srinivasaiah on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127711238/
6 maintenance throughout the lifetime of the petitioner.
Considering all these factors, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,50,000/- under this head, which shall not carry any interest.
SCCH-23 20.
EXPENSES INCURRED TOWARDS DAMAGES CAUSED TO THE VEHICLE:
PW.1 has deposed that in the accident his motorcycle was badly damaged and he has spent substantial amount towards its repair.

In order to substantiate this aspect he has produced estimation for damage repair total amounting to Rs.13,320/- and he has also produced 2-Vehicle repair Tax invoices issued by Anant Bajaj for Rs.13,320/- produced and same is exhibited at Ex.P11.
In fact Ex.P11 Invoice bills issued after lapse of 4 months from the date accident.
Further more on close perusal of Tax Invoice, under the Head of Billing Type - It was mentioned as Insurance.
Hence it is clear that he was claimed the amount from his own insurance company.
Be that as it may neither the author of Ex.P11 nor the mechanic who repaired the vehicle is examined.
Survey report is also not produced.
In this view of the matter, this Tribunal holds that petitioner is not entitled to any amount under this head.
SCCH-23 21.

The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 16,800-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain &
sufferings : 3,00,000-00 3
Loss of income during laid-up : 1,28,000-00 period
4 Medical expenses : 2,98,800-00 5 Loss of future income due to : 30,72,000-00 disability 6 Loss of future amenities & : 1,50,000-00 happiness 7

Future prospects :
2,00,000-00 8
Future medical and other : 1,50,000-00 incidental expenses 9 Expenses incurred towards - Nil - Damages caused to the vehicle Total 43,15,600-00 22.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
23. The respondent is stated to be the owner of the offending vehicle.
He has not produced any document to show that his vehicle had insurance coverage at the time of accident.
It is well settled that a person driving a vehicle is presumed to SCCH-23 have authority to do the same unless the contrary is proved.

In the absence of any contrary evidence in this regard and also considering the fact that the claimant has established that the accident was caused by the driver of the tractor and trailer, the respondent is vicariously liable to pay the compensation awarded by this Tribunal.

Hence he is liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a.,
from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :

ORDER The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.43,15,600/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., (Excluding future medical expenses) from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
SCCH-23
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of Two months from the date of award.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
